definition: Used in code reviews to approve a change.
exampleSentence: The senior developer replied LGTM, so I merged the pull request.

definition: Marks something that is not finished yet.
exampleSentence: I marked the pull request as WIP because the tests are still missing.

definition: Asks a reviewer to check a change again after updates.
exampleSentence: I fixed your comments, so PTAL when you have a minute.

definition: Introduces a very short summary of a long text.
exampleSentence: TL;DR: the release is delayed until Friday because of a bug.

definition: Used before giving your personal opinion.
exampleSentence: IMO we should fix the old bugs before adding new features.

definition: A polite way to give your opinion.
exampleSentence: IMHO the second design is easier for new users.

definition: Used when you think something is true but are not completely sure.
exampleSentence: AFAIK the server will be updated tonight, but please check with Ali.

definition: A very small, unimportant comment in a code review, often about style.
exampleSentence: My only comment is a nit about the variable name.

definition: A problem that stops work from continuing or a release from going out.
exampleSentence: The login bug is a blocker, so we cannot release today.

turkish: ne kadar işe yarar bilmem ama
definition: Used to offer information that may or may not be useful.
exampleSentence: FWIW, the same error happened to me last week after an update.

definition: Used when you are not completely sure about a memory.
exampleSentence: IIRC, we fixed this bug in the last sprint.

definition: Used to add extra information in a message.
exampleSentence: BTW, the client moved the meeting to Thursday.

definition: Used before saying what you really think.
exampleSentence: TBH, I think the deadline is too short for this feature.

definition: Says that you are away from your computer for a short time.
exampleSentence: I will be AFK for twenty minutes while I get lunch.

definition: Says that you will return in a moment.
exampleSentence: Sorry, my doorbell is ringing, BRB in two minutes.

definition: A private message sent to one person in a chat app.
exampleSentence: Send me a DM with the server password instead of posting it in the channel.

definition: Short for pull request, a request to review and merge code.
exampleSentence: I opened a PR with the bug fix this morning.

definition: A document that proposes an idea and asks the team for feedback.
exampleSentence: Ali wrote an RFC about moving our database to the cloud.

definition: A short reply that means you have seen and understood a message.
exampleSentence: When the manager asked us to update the docs, everyone replied ACK.

definition: Says that someone is working from home today.
exampleSentence: I am WFH today because the plumber is coming.

definition: Holiday or days off that you are paid for.
exampleSentence: I have five days of PTO left for this year.

definition: The end of the working week, usually Friday.
exampleSentence: Please send the final report to the client by EOW.

definition: The end of the working day.
exampleSentence: The client needs our answer by COB today.

definition: Thanks someone before they help you.
exampleSentence: Could someone review my code before lunch? TIA!

definition: Says that something is no longer important.
exampleSentence: NVM, I found the file in the shared folder.

definition: A short way to say you do not know something.
exampleSentence: IDK why the build failed, but I am looking into it.

definition: Asks someone to tell you something.
exampleSentence: LMK if you need help with the deployment tonight.

definition: Used when sharing something people may not have seen.
exampleSentence: ICYMI, the new security policy starts on Monday.

definition: Says that results may be different for other people.
exampleSentence: This setting made my laptop faster, but YMMV.

definition: A short way to agree with a plan.
exampleSentence: Ali suggested Friday for the release, and I replied SGTM.

definition: Used when a question or field does not apply.
exampleSentence: Write N/A in the form if you do not have a middle name.

definition: Used when information will be shared later.
exampleSentence: The location of the team dinner is still TBA.

definition: A report that explains why a problem happened and how to prevent it.
exampleSentence: After the outage, the team wrote an RCA for the management.

definition: GitLab's name for a pull request.
exampleSentence: In GitLab, you open an MR instead of a pull request.

definition: Used to start a short question in chat.
exampleSentence: QQ: does anyone know the password for the test server?

definition: Shows that you agree with a message or idea.
exampleSentence: Three colleagues replied +1 to the idea of a team lunch.

definition: Says that a change is ready to be released.
exampleSentence: The tests passed, so the team lead wrote ship it in the chat.

definition: Spending too much time on small, unimportant details.
exampleSentence: We spent an hour bikeshedding about the button color.

definition: Finding a bug by explaining your code line by line, even to an object.
exampleSentence: Rubber duck debugging helped me find the bug in five minutes.

turkish: asıl işten önce yapılan zincirleme küçük işler
definition: Doing many small tasks that you need before you can start the real task.
exampleSentence: Updating the tools before fixing the bug turned into a day of yak shaving.
